accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a finite alphabet and let $ be a separator symbol not in Σ. Can a one-way multihead deterministic finite automaton recognize the string-matching language {x$uxv | u, x, v are strings in Σ*}, that is, determine whether an input contains two occurrences of the same pattern x separated as x$uxv? Equivalently, can one-way multihead deterministic finite automata perform string matching?
accepted.context_brief: one-way multihead automata for string matching

evidence.quote: Question 1: Can a one-way multihead dfa perform string matching?
More specifically, can such an automaton recognize the language {x$uxvlu, x, v E E*}.

accepted.question_text: Fix a pattern string x. In the Boyer-Moore approach, one can imagine a deterministic finite automaton that remembers which parts of x need not be compared again after a mismatch when the pattern is shifted. What is the exact number of states such a Boyer-Moore automaton must have, or at least what are tight upper and lower bounds for that number as a function of |x| and the alphabet?

evidence.quote: Question 2: The number of states in a "Boyer-Moore dfa".

Knuth [19] suggested using a dfa that will "remember" those parts of the pattern that need not be compared. The question is to find the exact number, or alternatively close upper and lower bounds on the number of states such a dfa must have.

accepted.question_text: For string matching on an input of length n, can one design optimal parallel algorithms—meaning algorithms using p processors and time t with pt = O(n)—for larger processor ranges than were then known, specifically for ranges such as p ≤ n on a WRAM or p ≤ n/log n on a PRAM, while still solving the same string-matching problem efficiently?

evidence.quote: Recently, optimal parallel algorithms (those with pt = O(n), where p = number of processors, t = time) were developed for string matching for a wide range of values of p: on the WRAM for p <= n / log n and on the PRAM (for p <= n / log^2 n) ... Is it possible to design optimal parallel algorithms with a larger number of processors (e.g. p <= n on the WRAM, p <= n/ log n on the PRAM)?
